slides.text: I have a terrible, destructive habit of retreating when my anxiety peaks. When I panicked and canceled our highly anticipated third date an hour before he was supposed to pick me up, I assumed Liam would ghost me. I texted him a weak excuse about feeling sick, turned off my phone, and curled up on my sofa, crying silently at my own frustrating ability to self-sabotage a good thing.

Two hours later, there was a surprisingly soft knock at my apartment door. I froze. I peeked through the peephole to see Liam standing in the pouring rain. He didn't have flowers or grand, overwhelming romantic gestures. He had a battered copy of my favorite fantasy novel, a large thermal thermos of chamomile tea, and two heavy, incredibly soft fleece blankets tucked securely under his wet arm.

I opened the door, a completely mascara-smeared, anxious mess. He didn't try to kiss me or demand answers. 'I know you don't want to go out, and you probably don't want to talk,' he said gently, stepping inside the hallway. 'So, I'm just going to sit on the other end of your couch and read my book. You are never too complicated for me to show up.'
